summary: Los Padres lookout on Madulce Peak, built 1934 for the Santa Barbara National Forest; a 1972 windstorm destroyed the cab and a 2018 trip report describes foundations on the summit.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301, 10-foot open timber tower
facts.status_note: Cab destroyed in a 1972 windstorm and the rest later removed; a 2018 trip report describes foundations on the summit
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Los Padres National Forest

access.note: Inside the Dick Smith Wilderness (64,700 acres); no vehicle access to the summit is described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Trip reports describe a faint trail, with the turns near the summit mostly marked by cairns and flagging tape

events.note: Week-old fire moved north toward the peak and keeper Edward Decker left the post; the register says an earlier lookout burned, but the next day's paper said the burning reports were wrong
Built for the Santa Barbara National Forest as a 10-foot open timber tower to Plan BC-301
Trail to the lookout completed by late August 1934
Windstorm took off the roof, then the walls collapsed; the rest was removed afterward
Registered December 19, 2019; nominated by Brad Eells

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says an earlier lookout on the site was destroyed by fire in September 1932. The Oxnard Daily Courier's next-day report says the reports of the lookout burning were incorrect, so the register's claim is doubtful. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: PeakVisor says the lookout burned in the 1970s; the register says a 1972 windstorm destroyed it. The register's account is more detailed and is used, but the disagreement is unresolved. The register's claim of an earlier lookout destroyed in September 1932 is contradicted by the next day's newspaper. Today's condition rests on one 2018 trip report describing foundations; no survey, photo or later source was found. The record's 'removed 1972' is proposed as 'destroyed 1972' in corrections.
